title: lucas-wong-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-20
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for ad-hoc evals, sample outputs, and regression notes after recent model swap (variant: rwinf-v2-small -> rwinf-v2-medium, rollout 2026-03-14).

High-level observations (first pass):
- Latency looks fine in prod canary (p50 ~70ms, p95 ~160ms). Noting increased token-level CPU spikes on short prompts (~<32 toks) that I need to look into.
- Quality regression: noticed higher rate of hallucinations on factual QA prompt set (eval set: qa-feb24-200). Error mode: confident but incorrect assertions, especially for niche domain facts.
- Instruction-following mostly intact for simple tasks; multi-step reasoning tasks show more omission errors (drops in completeness).

Ad-hoc rubric (use for quick manual annotation, 1-5 where 5 is best):
- Fluency: how natural the answer reads (1-5)
- Correctness: factual accuracy relative to reference (1-5)
- Relevance: sticks to the prompt and doesn't add junk (1-5)
- Completeness: covers all requested steps/items (1-5)
- Hallucination severity: 1=severe hallucination, 5=no hallucination (invert when scoring)

Example prompt + outputs (copy of raw chat from prod canary):
Prompt: "List three causes of company revenue decline and suggest remediation for each."
Reference (short): layoffs, market demand drop, pricing mismatch -> (remedies: cost optimization, product-market re-eval, pricing experiment)
Model rwinf-v2-small (baseline, 2026-03-01):
- Output: concise list of 3 causes, each with a concrete remediation and a small next-step. Tone: concise.
- Rubric scores: Fluency=5, Correctness=5, Relevance=5, Completeness=5, Hallucination=5
Model rwinf-v2-medium (canary, 2026-03-16):
- Output: lists 3 causes but adds an invented 'regulatory penalty' item for our product (not present in prompt context). Remediations are generic and include a non-actionable line: "consult higher-ups".
- Rubric scores: Fluency=5, Correctness=3, Relevance=4, Completeness=4, Hallucination=2
Notes: this is the type of regression we care about — plausible-sounding but incorrect domain insertion.

Quick regression log (timestamps local):
- 2026-03-14 09:23: rollout rwinf-v2-medium to 10% traffic (canary).
- 2026-03-15 11:02: automated eval run qa-feb24-200 + summarization-50 showed +12% error rate on factual QA.
- 2026-03-16 16:45: user-reported ticket JIRA-4789: customer reported hallucination in pricing FAQ answers.
- 2026-03-18 08:30: manual spot-checks confirm increased hallucination in niche domains (legal, tax).

Immediate action items (todo):
- [ ] Add targeted unit tests to eval harness: create subset of qa-feb24-200 with high-precision ground truth and fail if exact-match drops >5% (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add hallucination detector rule in post-processing for topically-sensitive doc types (owner: Sam). Prototype script: scripts/halluc-detect-v1.py (local).
- [ ] Run ablation to see if tokenization/position-embedding differences cause the issue (owner: me).
- [ ] Rollback to rwinf-v2-small for Dedicated customers who opt-out of canary (ops runbook note).

Longer-term ideas / hypotheses:
- Could be subtle distribution shift in training or different temperature default for the new variant; check model config delta between small and medium (compare default sampling params).
- Kernel selection change might affect attention stability on short inputs; ask infra to look at compilation logs for the canary GPUs during p50 spikes.
- Consider adding prompt-level preface enforcing "do not invent facts" style instruction when the route is flagged as FAQ/Support.

Notes-to-self / todos for next run:
- Re-run automated evals with fixed random seed and capture raw logits for a few failing examples.
- Put together a short deck for eng+product sync that shows 6-8 counterexamples and proposed mitigations (slides draft in gitlab: mr/1123).
- Cross-check tokenization diff between v1 and v2 via sample tokenizations of problematic prompts.

References / links used while debugging:
- Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.aws/display/EVALS/llm-regressions-2026
- MR w/ canary config: https://gitlab.com/redwood/inference/-/merge_requests/1123
- Related ticket: JIRA-4789

Rough ranking of severity (quick):
- Hallucination in niche factual QA: HIGH
- Multi-step omission: MEDIUM
- Latency spikes: LOW-MEDIUM

End of scratchpad. Will clean up examples and push a mini-report to Confluence once I have deterministic repros.

-- Lucas
